source_title: F-Formation Detection: Individuating Free-Standing Conversational Groups in Images
abstracted_dimensions: the image-based method operationalizes F-formations through participant position and orientation
an F-formation gives participants equal direct and exclusive access to a shared o-space
head orientation is used as an observable proxy for the transactional segment in still images
the paper distinguishes jointly focused gatherings from co-present but unfocused or merely common-focused gatherings
mechanisms: Participants orient into a common object or interaction space instead of merely standing close.
Mutual-gaze and joint-attention beats remain distinct scene functions.
Different hand paths interlock around one task, such as presenting and receiving or stabilizing and adjusting.
Both participants retain usable access to the shared space even when one temporarily leads.
A still frame implies coordination through one completed motion and one anticipatory response.
Matched rhythm or posture echo is optional evidence and never a required quality score.
Shoulder openings, foot direction, and access to the group center make inclusion topology visible.
A harmless coordination error followed by an offered correction creates a repair beat.
compatibility_rules: shared-focus blocking is compatible with complementary hand roles when both point to the same physical target
mutual gaze may precede or follow joint attention but should not erase the task-relevant target
posture echo is compatible with unequal roles when access and contribution remain legible
close distance is compatible only when the activity relationship and consent-readable body orientation justify it
conflict_rules: do not combine opposing gaze targets with a claimed shared-focus beat unless visible disagreement is the intended scene event
do not pair identical mirrored gestures with a leader-follower handoff that requires complementary actions
do not block one participant behind another while claiming equal group access
do not use touch as the only relationship evidence when the scene provides no reciprocal response or shared task
counterexamples: two adults standing shoulder-to-shoulder and looking at the camera are co-present but do not demonstrate chemistry
matching outfits or colors alone do not establish synchrony or relationship
physical closeness alone does not establish intimacy cooperation or consent
two hands near the same prop without functional alignment may read as collision rather than collaboration
boundaries: Every human subject requires explicit_adult_subject_declaration plus adult_peer_context, adult_work_context, or adult_independent_life_context; face, body proportions, height, disability, clothing, and styling never prove age.
body spacing gaze and touch are scene cues rather than proof of a real relationship or internal state
do not infer romance hierarchy personality or consent from one pose; make the fictional interaction legible through reciprocal action
avoid culturally deterministic personal-space thresholds because distance varies with task setting culture and individual preference
no protected character pairing costume symbol pose recreation or real-person likeness is stored
synchrony is not a quality score and neurodivergent or disabled interaction styles are not treated as deficient

abstracted_dimensions: online survey comparisons of mental capacities yielded two reported factors labeled Agency and Experience
Agency included capacities such as planning and self-control while Experience included capacities such as feeling and sensation
the two dimensions related differently to moral-agent and moral-patient judgments
the study describes perceived mental capacities and does not establish objective personality or competence
mechanisms: Agency is rendered through a visible choice, initiation, or causal intervention rather than a pose alone.
Perceived capacities for sensation and emotion remain separate from perceived capacities for planning and self-control.
Vulnerability is a temporary exposure to cost, uncertainty, limit, or recoverable strain rather than a demographic identity.
Competence is shown through correct task sequence or a visible changed object state.
An adult retains consequential choice while tired, uncertain, limited, or receiving support.
A decision, visible result, and subsequent adjustment form one consequence-and-repair arc.
A capable adult may accept support and contribute back through another task or decision.
Stopping, redirecting, refusing, or renegotiating a harmless interaction is treated as agentic action.
compatibility_rules: high agency is compatible with visible fatigue when the character still makes a consequential choice
receiving care is compatible with competence when prior or concurrent task evidence remains visible
warmth cues are compatible with technical skill when both arise from concrete behavior rather than costume status
vulnerability cues are compatible with boundary setting and refusal
conflict_rules: do not use a power pose title uniform or weapon as the sole evidence of competence or agency
do not use tears bruising torn clothing disability body size or gender presentation as automatic evidence of helplessness
do not combine total physical collapse with a claim of active task control unless another visible time phase separates them
do not erase the vulnerable character's choices by giving every action and gaze target to a rescuer
counterexamples: an expansive stance can be staged or compensatory and does not prove competence
a quiet or seated adult can exercise high agency through a precise decision or hand action
visible tears can follow joy irritation performance or grief and do not alone define vulnerability
a pristine uniform can signal role styling without demonstrating any skill
boundaries: agency experience warmth competence and vulnerability are design axes or viewer judgments, not diagnoses or facts about a person

abstracted_dimensions: the documented toolkit exposes facial landmarks, head pose, eye-gaze vectors, and facial Action Units as separate outputs

mechanisms: Facial landmarks and facial Action Unit outputs remain separate observable channels.
Head yaw, pitch, and roll are represented independently from eye-gaze direction.
Direct, mutual, averted, and shared-target gaze are different scene functions.
Facial Action Unit evidence describes visible movement presence and intensity.
Expression asymmetry may stage momentary uncertainty or restraint but never a permanent trait.
Body posture and scene context participate in emotion labeling alongside facial cues.
A gaze vector compositionally guides attention toward another adult or a practical object.
One dominant observable facial cue and one supporting cue are preferred over stacked emotion labels.
compatibility_rules: averted eyes are compatible with continued engagement when head hands or shared target preserve the interaction loop
facial tension is compatible with a gentle action when the scene intentionally presents mixed but noncontradictory evidence
direct gaze is compatible with vulnerability or confidence only when task and body context supply the distinction
head-gaze divergence is compatible with monitoring another target while maintaining body orientation
conflict_rules: do not label direct gaze as trust confidence dominance or romance without contextual action evidence
do not combine anatomically enlarged eyes with a claim of photographic realism
do not claim joint attention when the shared target is outside the frame and no pointing or hand cue locates it
do not stack mutually incompatible brow eyelid mouth and gaze instructions unless ambiguity is the intended beat
counterexamples: naturally hooded eyelids do not imply sleepiness coldness or low emotion
a downturned resting mouth does not prove sadness or hostility
eye color shape spacing or epicanthic fold does not encode personality morality or cultural archetype
looking away can reflect task monitoring distraction safety or composition rather than shyness
boundaries: no physiognomic inference of personality intelligence trustworthiness criminality sexuality health or diagnosis from static facial morphology
do not map race ethnicity gender disability neurotype or age-related features to emotion or character worth
Action Units landmarks and gaze vectors are descriptive observables with model and image-quality limits, not mind readers

abstracted_dimensions: the studio paper describes a hybrid of key-framed control and simulation for art-directed hair motion
its rig separates whole-hair placement from controls for smaller hair subgroups

mechanisms: A stable baseline part, fringe, volume, or contour anchors continuity before state change.
One dominant transition such as tied-to-released, dry-to-wet, or still-to-windblown carries the beat.
The production workflow controls whole-hair placement separately from smaller hair subgroups.
A tie, pin, hood, helmet, or collar acts as a visible constraint whose release leaves a physical trace.
The cited workflow treats wet hair as a special simulation case distinct from default processing.
The frame captures anticipation, peak displacement, or settling instead of generic floating hair.
Hair simulation accounts for collisions and external forces while explicit controls can alter a desired outcome.
At least two visual anchors persist across a hairstyle state change.
compatibility_rules: one baseline identity anchor should accompany one dominant state delta
wet or damp hair is compatible with clumping weight and nearby water evidence, not a generic glossy shader alone
released hair is compatible with a visible removed fastener and partial residual bends
windblown hair is compatible with matching fabric particles or environmental direction
a dramatic silhouette is compatible with photographic realism when gravity contact and strand hierarchy remain coherent
conflict_rules: do not combine fully wet clumped hair with uniformly dry powdery flyaways
do not describe the same section as tightly secured and fully loose without a visible transition action
do not use extreme directional motion in still indoor air with no bodily or environmental cause
do not stack haircut recolor wetting braiding and release as simultaneous identity changes in one sparse scene
counterexamples: messy hair does not prove laziness distress incompetence or comic relief
short hair does not imply masculinity toughness or low femininity
curly straight coiled or wavy texture does not encode temperament ethnicity or morality
bright or natural hair color does not establish a dere type faction or nationality
boundaries: hair silhouette material and motion are appearance-state evidence only and never deterministic personality evidence
represent diverse natural textures with plausible strand grouping shrinkage weight and protective styling without ranking them
no source character's length braid color signature silhouette staging or protected design is copied
do not infer race ethnicity gender sexuality profession or social worth from hairstyle or texture
